ai.description: This 10–15 cm lizard features a flattened body and a long tail. Males display vibrant red heads and yellow-spotted black bodies during breeding, while females and juveniles are mottled brown.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the distinct, enlarged, and keeled scales on the nape and back, which form a prominent, crest-like ridge absent in other Indian agamid species.
ai.habitat: *Psammophilus dorsalis* inhabits rocky outcrops and boulder-strewn landscapes in the scrub jungles and dry deciduous forests of the Deccan Plateau, typically below 1,500m.
ai.behavior: The South Indian Rock Agama is a diurnal lizard that frequently performs "push-up" displays on exposed boulders to signal dominance and defend its territory from rivals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Psammophilus dorsalis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 5–8 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Psammophilus dorsalis* is endemic to southern India, primarily inhabiting rocky outcrops across the Western Ghats and Deccan Plateau at elevations up to 2,000 meters.
